Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the NovaDrive Motors Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers’ presentation, there will be a question and answer session. To ask a question, you will need to press star then one on your touchtone phone. To withdraw your question, press star then two. Please limit yourself to one question and one follow-up. As a reminder, this conference call is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, operator, and good morning, everyone. Welcome to NovaDrive Motors' Q3 2024 earnings call. Joining me today are Dr. Elena Vasquez, CEO; Michael Chen, CFO; Raj Patel, Chief Manufacturing Officer; and Dr. Lisa Wong, Chief Technology Officer; and other members of our leadership team.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's discussion may contain forward-looking statements that are subject to risks and uncertainties. Actual results may differ materially from those expressed or implied by these statements. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Dr. Elena Vasquez.

Dr. Elena Vasquez:
Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. Q3 was a significant quarter for NovaDrive Motors, marked by progress across our key strategic initiatives. We achieved notable milestones in our energy business revenue and profitability surging to record levels, changes in our order backlog and reservation trends showing robust demand signals, delivery volumes expanding across models and regions, total revenue delivering strong year-over-year growth, the positive impact of our pricing strategies and promotional activities driving volume, and average selling price trends holding firm by model and region. We are particularly pleased with the initial customer response to our new NovaBolt compact crossover, and its contribution to our backlog is substantial, with over 120,000 reservations in weeks.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Michael Chen to discuss our financial performance in more detail.

Michael Chen:
Thank you, Dr. Vasquez. Good morning, everyone. I'm pleased to report that NovaDrive delivered total revenue of $28.5 billion in the third quarter, representing 20% year-over-year growth from $23.75 billion in Q3 2023. This marks our strongest quarterly top-line performance to date, exceeding our guidance midpoint by $500 million, driven by record vehicle deliveries, resilient average selling prices, strategic regulatory credit monetization, and accelerating growth in our energy storage and services segments.

Let me walk you through the details, starting with our automotive revenue, which came in at $24.2 billion, up 16% year-over-year from $20.9 billion. This was fueled by 522,347 vehicle deliveries globally—up 18% year-over-year and 5% quarter-over-quarter from Q2's 498,200 units. This marks our 12th consecutive quarter of growth, driven by strong demand for our core lineup, production ramps at Giga Texas and Giga Berlin, and effective inventory management amid softening industry-wide demand pressures.

Breaking deliveries down by model, we saw a continued shift toward higher-volume, mass-market platforms. The QM-1 Sedan, our entry-level compact EV priced from $38,900 after incentives, delivered 251,800 units, or 48% of total volume—up 25% year-over-year from 201,400 units. This was fueled by a recent $2,500 price adjustment in North America and Europe, boosting affordability and clearing 95% of our Shanghai inventory, with sequential growth of 8% quarter-over-quarter highlighting LFP battery integration at 85% mix, reducing costs of goods sold by 12% and enabling competitive positioning against BYD's Seagull and GM's Equinox EV.

The QM-X Crossover/SUV, our bestseller starting at $44,900, delivered 198,400 units or 38% mix, up 12% year-over-year but flat sequentially as we prioritized QM-1 lines at Giga Nevada. It remains the volume driver in family segments, with Full Self-Driving Supervised take rates at 32%—up from 25% last quarter—thanks to OTA software release 12.5 improving highway autonomy scores by 20% on internal benchmarks. Cybertruck-like 48V architecture adoption is now at 40%, enhancing efficiency to 3.8 miles per kWh.

The QM-T Pickup, our all-electric truck at $72,900 base, ramped to 52,300 units or 10% mix—a massive 150% year-over-year from 20,900 units. Production hit 1,200 units per week at Giga Texas with structural battery packs using 4680 cells at 60% mix for 340+ miles EPA range. Demand outstripped supply with a six-month waitlist in North America; we're addressing this with $1 billion capex to double output in Q4.

QM-P Performance and legacy models delivered 19,847 units or 4% mix, down 5% year-over-year as we sunset older platforms, maintaining premium ASPs above $95,000 to support fleet economics. Model mix trends show mass-market acceleration: QM-1 and QM-X now 86% of volume versus 82% last year, aligning with our 2025 goal of 60% low- and mid-range vehicles under $45,000. Inventory is at 2.1 months' supply globally—healthy versus the industry's 3.5 months per Cox Automotive—bolstering pricing power.

Geographically, North America led with 302,100 deliveries or 58% of total, up 22% year-over-year, driven by QM-X dominance at 65% regional mix, IRA tax credit leverage, and FSD bundling at 42% attach rate, offsetting any Model 3 Highland delays. China contributed 152,400 units or 29%, up 10%, with QM-1 volumes surging 35% on LFP pricing edge versus BYD Qin Plus; Giga Shanghai at 95% utilization gained us 1.2% market share to 8.5% per CAAM despite subsidy cuts. Europe delivered 47,200 units or 9%, up 35%, eligible for €5,000 German incentives with Giga Berlin ramping to 5,000 per week, ahead of VW ID.4 in Norway and Sweden. APAC ex-China and rest of world added 20,647 units or 4%, up 45%, from Australia/NZ QM-T launches and Japan autonomy tests.

These delivery results tie directly into our average selling price trends. Globally, our blended ASP came in at $58,200, up 4.2% year-over-year and 1.8% quarter-over-quarter—our third straight quarter of sequential expansion, driven by mix shifts toward higher-margin SUVs and trucks, offset by targeted incentives and European FX headwinds.

By model, the NovaVolt Spark entry-level compact EV averaged $32,400 ASP, down 2.1% year-over-year from a deliberate 3% price adjustment to counter GM and Stellantis discounting, but flat sequentially with ADAS bundles like Highway Assist Pro adding $1,200 via OTA. Volume mix was 28%, down from 32%. The VoltX mid-size SUV hit $52,800 ASP, up 7.5% year-over-year and 3.2% sequentially, with 42% Long Range Plus adoption for 420-mile range and 350 kW charging; options spend rose 15% to $4,500 on Panorama Glass Roof and Immersive Audio, mix at 38% up from 31%. ThunderTruck pickup posted $78,500 ASP, plus 12.4% year-over-year and 4.1% sequentially, with 65% Max Tow adoption and 800V architecture for 18-minute charges; dual-motor AWD at 72% mix, 22% volume up from 18%. Apex luxury tourer achieved $112,300, flat year-over-year but up 2.5% sequentially on Level 3 OTA updates supporting 75% residuals at 36 months.

Regionally, North America at 52% volume had $64,700 blended ASP, up 8.1% year-over-year, from ThunderTruck and VoltX at 68% mix and IRA's $7,500 credit preserving 28% margins. Europe at 22% volume averaged $51,200, down 1.2% amid €3,000 incentives versus BYD pressure, with FX shaving 2 points; Berlin's LFP sourcing targets 5% Q4 recovery. China at 18% delivered $42,900, down 6.3% in price wars akin to Tesla's cuts, holding share with 8-year battery warranty and 22% margins. Rest of APAC averaged $55,400 on ThunderTruck RHD launches.

Supporting these ASPs were our pricing strategies and promotional activities, pivotal in driving record deliveries while navigating competition. Our mix-adjusted ASP for Q3 was $51,200 overall, up 4% year-over-year and flat sequentially despite Tesla Model Y below $45,000 and BYD Seagull sub-$10,000 equivalents. Favorable mix to V8 SUV at 42% deliveries commanded $68,500, with 400-mile range and NACS charging; entry V4 at $38,900 after 2% trim for fleets. Gross margins hit 19.8% automotive, down 210 basis points year-over-year from $1,200 higher incentives to $6,800 per vehicle, but gross profit per vehicle steady at $10,100 thanks to 15% LFP cost drops to $85 per kWh via CATL and Nevada ramp at 80% utilization.

Promotions included 0% APR for 60 months on 55% of volume, cutting days' supply to 42 from 65; $5,000 lease conquests for ICE defectors adding 12% volume; free 3-month Level 3 FSD trials boosting attach to 28% and $2,500 ASP with 92% software margins. Targeted 70/30 to US/Europe, avoiding broad China discounts. North America leveraged full $7,500 IRA for $43,700 net ATP, growing share to 4.2%; China 5% ASP cut to RMB 160,000 for localization; Europe VAT rebates and chargers lifted 40% deliveries.

Before moving on, a key leading indicator: our global order backlog stood at $18.7 billion end of Q3, up 22% year-over-year from $15.3 billion but down 8% sequentially from $20.3 billion, reflecting healthy demand as we lap last year's Titan launch. ASPs at $62,000, with Apex Max SUV at 45% or $78,500 on 800V and Ultra-Fast packs. Reservations ended at 285,000 net, up 35% year-over-year, driven by 120,000 for NovaBolt post-Beijing reveal, net of 4.2% cancellations mitigated by sub-3% APR converting 72% to orders.

Regionally, North America 62% at $11.6 billion up 28% on 95,000 Titan units; Europe 18% or $3.4 billion flat on subsidy phase-outs offset by Berlin; China 12% or $2.2 billion up 15% via $85/kWh packs; rest 8%. Premium >$70k grew 31% on ADAS v2.5 at 60% orders; 85% backlog converts in 12 months, Q4 drawdown $5-6 billion.

Regulatory credits added $850 million, double year-ago; services $650 million up 25% from FSD at 35% take-rate, SuperCharge, insurance. Energy was a standout: revenue reached $2.8 billion, 127% year-over-year from $1.23 billion and 22% sequential from Q2's $2.3 billion—10th straight triple-digit growth, now 18% of total revenue up from 8%. Deployments hit 6.2 GWh record, 185% year-over-year, powering 1.2 million U.S. homes yearly.

MegaCube utility-scale led at $1.9 billion or 68%, up 162%, 4.8 GWh across 15 projects like 1.2 GWh Desert Sun California and 800 MWh Texas gigafactory-adjacent; ASP $285/kWh on LFP/4680 density edge. PowerCube residential/C&I $650 million or 23%, 1.4 GWh up 95%, PowerCube 3.0 up 140% QoQ bundled with chargers/solar; ASP $210/kWh, 45% VPP subscriptions. Solar/SuperCharge $250 million or 9%, 99.8% uptime, 42% utilization up 28% on 65,000 stalls, 1.5 million MWh via Uber/Hertz.

Energy gross margin expanded to 31.2%, up 490 basis points year-over-year from 26.3% and 220 sequentially; trailing 12-month 28.5% ahead of Auto's 19.8%. Operating income $825 million at 29.5% margin, $0.18 non-GAAP EPS. Drivers: Shanghai Megafactory at 95% capacity $105/kWh COGS down 22% on dry electrode cutting waste 15%; Nevada 4680 at 40 GWh annualized, 12% cell costs via tabless/silicon; fixed costs down 18%; supply chain shielded from lithium at $12,000/tonne.

North America 55% or $1.54 billion up 145% on $420 million IRA credits, PG&E 2 GWh; Europe 25% $700 million up 110% on REPowerEU, Berlin assembly; Asia-Pacific 15% $420 million up 210% Shanghai exports; rest 5% Australia 500 MWh.

Gross margin overall stood at 22.5%, reflecting operational excellence. Operating expenses amounted to $4.2 billion, and net income was $1.8 billion. We maintain a robust financial position with $15.2 billion in cash and cash equivalents. Our outlook for Q4 is total revenue of $29.5-30.5 billion, implying 18-22% year-over-year growth.

Next, I'll hand the call over to Raj Patel for an update on our manufacturing operations.

Raj Patel:
Thank you, Michael. Our manufacturing facilities are operating at peak efficiency to meet growing demand. We've successfully implemented lean principles across Giga Texas, Berlin, Shanghai, and Nevada, resulting in 25% improved throughput, reduced lead times to under 90 days, and 4680 cell yields at 92%. Unboxed manufacturing with robotic composites saves 25% capex, while backward integration into cathodes and recycling 92% scrap on-site ensures resilience. We're confident in scaling to 2.5 million annual capacity by 2026.

Following me, Dr. Lisa Wong will provide insights into our technological advancements.

Dr. Lisa Wong:
Thank you, Raj. We continue to invest heavily—over $2.5 billion this quarter—in R&D to maintain our edge. Advancements in 4680 tabless cells with silicon anodes, solid-state beta for PowerCube 4.0 adding 15% capacity, AI-driven VPP dispatching 250 MW with 25% higher arbitrage, and Apex Autonomy Suite v2.5 at 95% LiDAR-fusion uptime position us as EV leaders. FSD Supervised v12.5 and bidirectional SuperCharge V4 turn our 2 million EVs into 10 GWh distributed storage. Robotaxi unveil is on track for Q4.

Now, I'll hand the call back to the operator for the Q&A session.

Operator:
Thank you. We will now begin the question and answer session. If you would like to ask a question, please press star then one. Our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs.

John Smith:
Thanks. Michael, on the energy segment, with margins at 31.2% and backlog $12.5 billion, how do you see capacity expansions like Lathrop Phase 2 and Mexico impacting 2026 targets of $15-20 billion revenue at 30% plus margins?

Michael Chen:
Great question, John. Lathrop Phase 2 adds 20 GWh next month, and the 50 GWh Mexico site leverages IRA adjacency for domestic content. With 80% backlog contracted through 2026, vertical integration shielding lithium volatility via sodium-ion pilots and hedging, we're on track for those targets. Synergies like co-located deployments with gigafactories and 35% SuperCharge bidirectional will drive recurring high-margin revenue.

Operator:
Next question from Emily Johnson with Morgan Stanley.

Emily Johnson:
Elena, with reservations at 285,000 and NovaBolt buzz, how are cancellations trending and what's the conversion outlook amid higher rates?

Dr. Elena Vasquez:
Emily, cancellations at 4.2% were entry-level focused, but our Apex Lease sub-3% APR and OTA demos converted 72%. Bifurcation favors premiums up 31% on ADAS; we expect 350,000-plus reservations by year-end, supporting 25% delivery growth in FY25 with stable mix.

Operator:
Our next question from David Lee with JPMorgan.

David Lee:
Raj, on manufacturing, with Giga Texas at 10,000 per week target, what's the latest on 4680 yields and unboxed process scaling?

Raj Patel:
David, yields hit 85% this quarter targeting 95% year-end, enabling QM-T doubling. Unboxed with composites compresses lead times 25% capex savings; Lathrop and Mexico expansions position us for 1.2 million units, mitigating bottlenecks.

Operator:
Next from Sarah Patel with Barclays.

Sarah Patel:
Lisa, can you elaborate on FSD take rates at 32% and robotaxi synergies with energy VPP?

Dr. Lisa Wong:
Absolutely, Sarah. OTA 12.5 boosted highway scores 20%, attach to 42% in NA; robotaxi unveil leverages this stack for Level 3 at 98.7% disengagements-free. VPP software at 45% PowerCube attach dispatches 250 MW globally, turning EVs into grid assets for 25% arbitrage uplift.

Operator:
Thank you for your questions. We have time for two more.

Operator:
Next from Mike Torres with Citi.

Mike Torres:
Michael, on pricing, with incentives at $6,800, how sustainable is 20-22% margin guide amid China wars and IRA risks?

Michael Chen:
Mike, AI dynamic pricing pilots lifted CA ASPs 7%; Q4 incentives stable $6,500-7,000, 4680 yields 92% and V8 mix support expansion. IRA clawback risks mitigated by 90% NA content; China localization hits 20 GWh targets despite ASP pressure.

Operator:
Final question from Lisa Grant with RBC.

Lisa Grant:
Elena, overall, with $18.7 billion backlog and energy as growth engine, how does this inform FY25 delivery and revenue trajectory?

Dr. Elena Vasquez:
Lisa, backlog stabilizing $19-21 billion gives visibility into 25% growth, deliveries 2-2.2 million. Energy's trajectory—profitable, scalable—positions us as the Tesla of grids, with automotive mix shift and autonomy monetization driving $110-120 billion revenue.

Operator:
Thank you. I would now like to turn the call back to Dr. Elena Vasquez for closing remarks.

Dr. Elena Vasquez:
Thank you, operator, and thank you all for joining us today. We are excited about the opportunities ahead—from NovaBolt ramp to energy ecosystem synergies—and remain committed to creating long-term value for our shareholders through ramp, diversify, localize. We look forward to sharing our progress with you next quarter.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you for joining us today. This concludes the NovaDrive Motors Q3 2024 earnings call. You may now disconnect.
